verdicts.evidence: FALSE GREEN, verified by exit code. Applied on m4 (single defect: `file:code/deleted-a.ts<U+2028>; file:code/b.ts`): `check --strict --json` went from **exit 1 to exit 0**, conformance 1 -> 0, and the violation `Floor · tools-scope-atomicity · typed pointer does not resolve: file:code/deleted-a.ts — update it or remove the row` disappeared entirely. Re-observed on m2, where the same mutant removed TWO refusals (conformance 10 -> 8): `file:code/deleted-a.ts` (U+2028 separator) and `file:code/deleted-a2.ts` (CR separator). Mechanism as observed, not as read: when a chunk ends in a line terminator, POINTER_PREFIX's `(\S.*)$` cannot reach `$` (`.` excludes line terminators), the chunk yields no match and the pointer is dropped silently — the row still reads as typed and the cited file is never opened. This is the RWD-2026-0006 family: a pointer that looks precise and verifies nothing. Reachable because `readManifest` only trims the ENDS of a cell, so a terminator sitting before a `;` survives into the chunk. The missing test: a cell whose first pointer is followed by CR or U+2028 and then `; <second pointer>` must still refuse the first pointer's missing file.

Applied on m2, m3 and m6. Exit code, violation count and all evidence counters unchanged; the `problem` strings became `typed pointer does not resolve: test: — update it or remove the row` and `typed pointer test: — test named "the "guard" path" not found in the file` (baseline: the full `test:code/test/nope.test.ts` / `test:code/test/pointers.test.ts::the`). Splitting on `/\S/` instead of `/\s/` makes `rest.split(...)[0]` the empty string, so the printed pointer collapses to its scheme.
verdicts.argument: 484-cell sweep: no field other than `raw` changes on any cell, and the pointer count never moves. `raw` on a `test:` pointer reaches only the violation sentence. Same class as the mutant above: the refusal stops naming its subject; the verdict is untouched.

verdicts.evidence: Applied on m2 and m6. `check --strict --json` kept exit 1, the same violation count and every evidence counter, but two `problem` strings lost the pointer they name: `typed pointer does not resolve: test:code/test/nope.test.ts — update it or remove the row` became `typed pointer does not resolve:  — update it or remove the row`, and `typed pointer test:code/test/pointers.test.ts::the — test named …` became `typed pointer  — test named …`. On m3 the same, on the `::` names no test row.
verdicts.argument: Over the 484-cell sweep this mutant changes NO pointer field other than `raw`: `path`, `line`, `symbol`, `testName`, `adrId`, `symbolDeclared`, `testNameDeclared` and `malformed` are identical on every cell, and the pointer count never moves. `raw` on a `test:` pointer is only ever interpolated into a violation sentence, so no verdict, count or seal can move. It is still a defect in ADR-0046's own terms — a refusal that no longer names what it refuses, in the ADR-0030 machine contract a CI parses. Its fix is an assertion on the message, not a verdict test.

verdicts.evidence: Four siblings KILLED here (the `pathShaped` condition of the `::` branch, the block it guards, the echo of the branch without `::`, the echo of a misspelt `adr:`), two of them on a site that NO input of the probe reached before it was widened — there are two `if (!pathShaped(tpath))`. What remains is on anchoring variants unreachable by the grammar: `/^ADR-?\d/i` against `/ADR-?\d/i` on an operand already split at the first whitespace, and `/\S/` where the split guarantees there is no whitespace. METHOD OF THIS PASS (identical for every verdict below, closed on 2026-09-18). The mutant is APPLIED to the build, a behaviour probe calls the product on inputs that reach the mutated line, and a canonical digest of 250+ observations is compared: pointer grammar over 34 cells, manifest sections over 12 documents (renamed heading, lowercase, deep, last, duplicated, inside a code block, unclosed block), decision journals over 16 layouts, nine real missions read by evidenceReport/evidenceBreakdown/collectSealableEvidence/requiresLedger/prosePointerLedger/computeVerdict in strict AND non-strict, and the exact bounds of the signature guard (30, 119, 120, 121, 511, 512, 513). COVERAGE VERIFIED: the 56 instructed survivors are all on a line the probe EXECUTES, measured by NODE_V8_COVERAGE taking the innermost range (the first version marked 1540 lines out of 1540 and measured nothing). SENSITIVITY PROVEN: on this same pass, 20 mutants moved the probe and are now KILLED by tests written after reading the difference — so the instrument does tell what changes from what does not. The probe was wrong six times before it was right, and its failure mode was always to answer "equivalent": branches not reached, messages cut at 200 characters, verdict truncated at 4000, wrong mutated occurrence chosen. Each correction surfaced changing mutants that would have been filed wrongly.

verdicts.evidence: Applied on the self-gate, on m2, on m3, on m4, on m5 and on m6: the `check --strict --json` payload was byte-identical to baseline every time (m2: exit 1 -> 1, conformance 10 -> 10, every evidence counter unchanged; m3, built specifically to put `::` and whitespace in every relative position, likewise). On the 484-cell sweep — which includes `test:a.ts::n`, `test:a.ts:: n`, `test:a.ts::`, `test:a b.ts::n`, `test:x y::z`, `test:a.ts :: n`, `test:  ::n`, `test:` and the same shapes embedded in prose — the parsed pointer objects were identical on all 484, field for field.
verdicts.argument: The comparison is only ever evaluated on the third leg of `sep !== -1 && (firstWs === -1 || sep < firstWs)`: reaching it requires `sep !== -1` AND `firstWs !== -1`, since `firstWs === -1` short-circuits the disjunction to true before the comparison runs. On that path `sep = rest.indexOf("::")`, so `rest[sep]` is the character `:`; and `firstWs = rest.search(/\s/)`, so `rest[firstWs]` is a whitespace character. `:` is not a whitespace character, therefore `sep === firstWs` is unreachable for every possible input string, and `<` and `<=` return the same boolean wherever the expression is evaluated. No mission can distinguish them because no Evidence cell can make a colon be whitespace.

verdicts.evidence: Applied on m2. `check --strict --json` gained a violation the baseline did not have: `Floor · hexa-architecture · typed pointer test:code/test/pointers.test.ts:: — test named "the guard fails closed" — second half of the case" not found in the file` (conformance 10 -> 11). Baseline parses that cell's test name as `the guard fails closed`, finds it in code/test/pointers.test.ts and says nothing; with the mutant the quoted-name matcher no longer matches, the fallback keeps the trailing prose, and the gate goes looking for a sentence nobody wrote. A row the operator wrote correctly is refused. Confirmed on the 484-cell sweep: this mutant changes the parsed `testName` — a value the gate searches file content for — on 9 to 12 cells. Also observed on m6, where it changed the payload (`OBSERVABLE: json`).

Applied on m2 and m3. On m2, `check --strict --json` gained the violation `Floor · provider-no-crash-missing-env · typed pointer test:code/test/pointers.test.ts:: — test named "  spaced name" not found in the file` (conformance 10 -> 11) where the baseline was silent: the cell `test:code/test/pointers.test.ts::  spaced name` parses to the name `spaced name`, which the file declares, and without the trim the gate searches for the name with its two leading spaces still attached. On m3 the same effect on the cell `test:…:: plain` (searched name became ` plain`). 33 of the 484 sweep cells change the parsed `testName`. A green row goes red on whitespace the operator cannot see.

Applied on m2. `check --strict --json` gained `Floor · state-event-sourcing · typed pointer test:code/test/pointers.test.ts::'l'invariant — test named "Stryker was here!l'invariant tientStryker was here!" not found in the file` (conformance 10 -> 11) where the baseline was silent. The replacement string of the quote-strip is substituted into the test name, so the value the gate searches for is corrupted — 21 of 484 sweep cells change `testName`. Verdict-capable: any row whose test name starts or ends with a quote character goes red.

verdicts.evidence: Measured on `cells`: `test:code/reports/junit.xml::` (empty name) is refused either way, same exit 1, same counters; the problem string `typed pointer test:code/reports/junit.xml:: — the \`::\` names no test` becomes `typed pointer test:code/reports/junit.xml — …` in --json, text and the witness `problem`. Identical on `cells2` and on `seal-plain`. The literal is the echo of an empty `::`. The previous filing of this mutant (on the pre-echoTestName line) said equivalent; the message change is measured, so it is re-filed display-only. METHOD (2026-11-04, report of CI run 41823709461 on main a3a614f, dist/lib/evidence.js byte-identical to the report's embedded source). Each mutant was spliced into the built file at its report offsets (original text checked before the splice, the file read back after it), then a fixed battery of real CLI runs (`node dist/cli.js check ... --no-color --path .`, Node 24.22.1) was replayed on fresh copies of an `init --example` mission (request-triage) and every exit code, stdout, stderr and written file (lock, witness) was compared byte for byte with the pristine build. verdicts.argument: The mutated operand is the left half of `symbol !== undefined && /\s/.test(symbol)`. When `symbol` is a string, `symbol !== undefined` is already `true`, so replacing it by `true` changes nothing. When `symbol` is `undefined`, the original short-circuits the conjunction to `false`; the mutant instead evaluates `/\s/.test(undefined)`, and `RegExp.prototype.test` coerces its argument with ToString, giving the seven-letter string `"undefined"`, which contains no whitespace — so the test is `false` and the conjunction is `false` too. Both forms therefore select the same branch of the ternary on every input. `symbol` is `string | undefined` by construction (it is assigned only from `quoted[3] || undefined` and from `token.slice(hash + 1) || undefined`), so `undefined` is the only non-string value it can hold and no other coercion is reachable; the regex has no `g` flag, so `test` has no side effect either. No mission can distinguish them.
